title: Exec weekly update — In-console Usage Insights (cost drivers by route) — Week of 2026-02-17
body:
Owner: Paula Mendes (PM)  |  Sponsor: Marissa Cole (Console)

Summary (1–2 mins)
- We are on track for a staged beta of Usage Insights (route + model cost drivers) in early/mid March, with GA targeted for early April, assuming we close two main risks: (1) route cardinality guardrails at ingestion + query and (2) export job performance limits + audit/RBAC completion.
- Big win this week: end-to-end route dimension propagation is working in staging, and the “Top routes by spend” view is rendering with realistic internal dogfood traffic.

What shipped / progress this week
Product/Design
- Design for route list + route detail is effectively frozen for beta scope (table-first with fast filters + deltas vs prior period). We kept treemap as a future exploration (not in beta).
- Empty states and “Unknown route” education copy drafted (ties to DevEx route-tagging guidance).

Engineering
- Telemetry: Route dimension is plumbed through request context → metering events in staging, including fallback/routing events capturing the original route identifier.
- Aggregations: Hourly + daily rollups are generating for internal orgs; validation is in progress against existing cost totals (expected small deltas from late-arriving events).
- API: Route list endpoint (top spend) is functional with pagination and core filters (time range, environment, region, org/project, deployment mode). Query cost guardrails are partially implemented.
- Console: Route insights page behind feature flag is working in staging, including basic charting and filter state.

Security/Compliance
- Audit event fields for export creation/download have been reviewed in concept; implementation is in progress alongside RBAC checks.

Key risks / watch items
1) Cardinality risk (route dimension)
- Why it matters: If customers pass high-cardinality values (e.g., user IDs, UUIDs, full URLs), the route dimension can blow up aggregates and degrade query performance/cost.
- Current status: We have an ADR and normalization rules drafted; enforcement is not fully in place yet.
- Mitigations in flight:
  - Normalize + cap route length; allowlist characters; collapse whitespace; enforce reserved “unknown/other” buckets.
  - Budget-based safeguards: per-org route cardinality thresholds, and defensive rollups/hashing once threshold exceeded.
  - Console guidance + docs: “Route naming do’s/don’ts” and SDK examples.
- Exec ask: alignment that we will hard-fail/roll up routes that exceed cardinality policy (even if it means some customer routes appear as “other”). This is required to keep the feature reliable at scale.

2) Export performance + guardrails
- Why it matters: Exports are the #1 enterprise request but can cause timeouts and operational load if unconstrained.
- Current status: Export flow is being built; we still need final guardrails (max rows/time range, server-side pagination vs job chunking) and clear UI/error messaging.
- Proposed guardrails for beta/GA:
  - Time range limit (e.g., 31 days) for a single export job by default, with admin override for Dedicated/Private only.
  - Size caps (rows and/or uncompressed bytes) with explicit “narrow your filters” error.
  - Export job queue concurrency per org + backoff.

3) Freshness vs accuracy (invoice reconciliation)
- Why it matters: Exec + customers will compare dashboard totals to invoices; we will have discrepancies due to late-arriving metering events, caching attribution, and retention windows.
- Current status: We have draft “known issues” messaging and a plan to display “data updated as of” timestamps.
- Plan: For GA we will message “operational insights” vs “billing statement,” plus a “compare to prior period” view rather than hard promises on exact reconciliation.

4) RBAC / tenant isolation for exports
- Why it matters: Export endpoints are higher risk than UI views; must enforce org/project scoping and produce auditable evidence.
- Current status: Security review is underway; implementation is in progress.

Beta / GA plan and expected ship date
- Beta target: Week of 2026-03-10 (design partners + internal dogfood), behind feature flag.
- GA target: Week of 2026-04-07.
- GA gating criteria (high level):
  - Cardinality enforcement enabled by default + documented
  - Export job limits + audit logging + RBAC complete
  - API p95 latency within budget under load test (Top routes + route detail)
  - Support readiness: FAQ + known issues + canned responses (invoice mismatch, unknown route)

Resourcing / decisions needed
1) Short-term eng help (2–3 weeks) for export hardening
- Ask: 1 additional backend engineer to pair with export work (job queue + size/time-range guardrails + retry logic).
- Rationale: export is on the critical path for enterprise adoption and is the highest operational risk area.

2) SRE/Observability bandwidth for pre-GA monitoring
- Ask: dedicated review time from Allison Grant (or delegate) to finalize alert thresholds + dashboards for pipeline lag, export job success rate, and API p95.
- Rationale: we’ve seen “incident-adjacent” behavior in internal load tests; need confidence before widening beta.

3) Product decision: strict route policy enforcement
- Confirm we will enforce normalization + rollups/hashing when thresholds are exceeded, and we will not add customer-configurable custom dimensions in initial GA.

Next week focus
- Finish route normalization + cardinality guardrails (ingest + query).
- Implement export audit events + RBAC checks end-to-end.
- Run a targeted load test on “Top routes” queries with realistic org sizes + route counts; validate caching strategy.
- Finalize customer-facing limitations language (docs + console tooltip copy) around freshness and invoice mismatch.

Open questions (for visibility)
- Do we want different export limits by deployment mode (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private) at GA, or keep a single conservative default?
- For “Unknown route,” do we default to gateway-derived path patterns for customers without SDK tagging, or keep it explicit to encourage proper tagging?
